nodes.label: Crab subagent avatar
nodes.rationale: Each subagent is drawn as a pixel-art crab with a distinct hat or accessory and a colored progress bar, so agents are distinguishable at a glance.

nodes.label: Two-pane layout
nodes.rationale: Log or conversation text sits on the left while the right column stacks one crab row per agent, separating history from live status.

nodes.label: Responsive layout breakpoints
nodes.rationale: The band is checked across many terminal sizes (columns by rows) to find where crabs, text and dividers stop fitting and the layout must switch to a compact form.

nodes.label: Narrow band layout
nodes.rationale: Below roughly 45 columns the band drops sprites and keeps only text, so the status stays readable on very narrow terminals.

nodes.label: Wide band layout
nodes.rationale: On wide terminals the band spreads the crab row across the full width with the divider and status line below it.

nodes.label: Animated Crab Subagent
nodes.rationale: Each Claude Code subagent is drawn as a small pixel crab that animates through frames, so a glance at the panel shows how many agents are running.

nodes.label: Costume and Accessory System
nodes.rationale: Hats and props (helmets, cowboy hats, hard hats, chef hats, crowns, caps) are layered on the same base crab. This lets users tell agents apart by costume without reading names.

nodes.label: Status Indicator Overlays
nodes.rationale: Small overlays on the crab (red exclamation marks, sparkles, colored badges) mark agent state such as attention needed, active work or done. The state is visible even when the text panel is hidden.

nodes.label: Agent Detail View
nodes.rationale: Drill-down view for one subagent: a large crab portrait with its costume, colored progress-style rows and text lines for that agent's activity.

nodes.label: Terminal Panel Layout
nodes.rationale: Two-column terminal panel with a left log/text pane and a right pixel-art pane, plus a bottom status band. Keeps the crab visuals inside the terminal without taking over the main conversation.

nodes.label: Subagent Roster List
nodes.rationale: Overview list of all subagents, one row per agent with a small crab avatar and a status line, so several agents can be monitored at once.

nodes.label: CrabBus Sprite Sheet (Dark Theme)
nodes.rationale: Art sheet on a near-black background showing the orange crab sprite in many costume and state variants arranged in a grid of animation frames. Used to check sprite legibility against the dark terminal theme.

nodes.label: CrabBus Sprite Sheet (Light Theme)
nodes.rationale: Same sprite grid as the dark sheet on an off-white background. Shows the crab set re-rendered for light terminals; outlines and dark accessories are kept so the sprites stay readable on both themes.

nodes.label: Agent Detail View Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Terminal UI screenshot: a left text/log pane, a right pane with one large crab portrait and its status lines, and a bottom status band. Shows the drill-down view for a single subagent.

nodes.label: Subagent List View Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Terminal UI screenshot: the same layout as the detail view, but the right pane lists several subagents, each with a crab avatar in a different hat and a short status line. Shows the overview roster.

nodes.label: Subagent costume roster
nodes.rationale: Subagent crabs are dressed in costumes (hats, outfits, themed sets such as Christmas or French) that encode identity or activity. This is the visual identity layer of subagents.

nodes.label: Crab mascot
nodes.rationale: The orange, crowned pixel crab is the project's recurring character. It is the same sprite used for the main agent and each subagent, and it appears in the logo, both wordmarks and the social preview.

nodes.label: Starfield banner backdrop
nodes.rationale: Animated dark starfield with dim pixel stars and a thin floor rail. Acts as a quiet ambient backdrop so the wordmark and crab row stay the focus of the banner.

nodes.label: Reading state crew strip
nodes.rationale: Seven costumed crabs (astronaut, detective, engineer, chef, pilot, pirate, propeller) under a READING header. Shows the costume roster used for the reading activity state.

nodes.label: Working state crew strip
nodes.rationale: Five costumed crabs (capybara, fisher, french, dino, christmas) under a WORKING header. Shows that costumes are grouped per activity state and that custom sets are possible.

nodes.label: CrabBus logo
nodes.rationale: Square icon: a crowned orange crab mascot with a thought bubble and trailing dots, framed by an orange border. Brand mark for the project.

nodes.label: CrabBus social preview card
nodes.rationale: Hero card combining the CrabBus wordmark, the tagline 'Observability for Claude Code subagents', and a row of seven costumed crabs. Intended as the shareable link preview image.

nodes.label: CrabBus wordmark (dark variant)
nodes.rationale: Horizontal lockup of the mascot and 'CrabBus', with the 'Bus' letters in dark ink, so it reads on light backgrounds.

nodes.label: CrabBus wordmark (light variant)
nodes.rationale: Horizontal lockup of the mascot and 'CrabBus', with the 'Bus' letters in cream, so it reads on the dark backgrounds used by the project.

nodes.label: Parallel subagent orchestration
nodes.rationale: One Claude Code session launches several background subagents in a single message. CrabBus makes that parallel fan-out observable as crabs in a panel.

nodes.label: Plan stage progress
nodes.rationale: Subagents report a multi-stage plan through bus_step. The detail view shows the current stage as a pager (for example 2/3) and the current action as text, so progress is visible per agent.

nodes.label: Subagent status states
nodes.rationale: Each subagent is classified into working, thinking, waiting, blocked or done, and the panel shows counts per state. The status vocabulary drives the panel and the crab animations.

nodes.label: Card drawing (drawAgent, drawMaster)
nodes.rationale: One crab in one costume doing one mood on a fixed 18 x 14 pixel card, so every agent has the same footprint and the card can be tested in isolation.

nodes.label: Preview tool (tools/preview.ts)
nodes.rationale: Renders scenes to PNG with the same half-block encoding so art can be reviewed without launching Claude Code; --design runs the fit check and shows the actions on dark and light backgrounds.

nodes.label: Scene composition (layout and compose)
nodes.rationale: layout decides what fits and compose draws it; both are pure, and callers pass now and the tick so output is deterministic under test.

nodes.label: Adaptive band layout
nodes.rationale: The band falls back to one colored text line when it cannot fit two cards of width or 8 rows, and extra agents are counted in the master label instead of taking a card, so narrow terminals still show status.

nodes.label: Half-block cells
nodes.rationale: One terminal cell holds two stacked pixels (upper half block, foreground over background), so an 18 x 14 sprite takes 18 columns and 7 rows and keeps every pixel's exact color, without depending on terminal image protocols.

nodes.label: Mood resolution per frame
nodes.rationale: The highest-priority action whose condition the recorded facts meet wins; falling back to walk keeps a crab moving when nothing specific is known.

nodes.label: One-shot plays and passes
nodes.rationale: A play starts when its condition becomes true, so a spin or kick does not restart every frame; passes between crabs are capped at MAX_PASSES so a ball never bounces forever.

nodes.label: Golden pixel tests
nodes.rationale: Pixel fingerprints pin the built-in costumes and actions, so an art or rig change fails a test instead of surprising the user in the terminal.

nodes.label: Open: second skin pack
nodes.rationale: A second set of sprites from CC0 sprite sheets, pending a license check of each sheet.

nodes.label: Paint timer (fps and reduceMotion)
nodes.rationale: A $.clock.every timer drives repaints at fps (default 6, clamped to 1-10); reduceMotion drops to one frame per second, so motion can be turned off without losing status.

nodes.label: clawd-actor prior art
nodes.rationale: Pure scene functions on an AbovePrompt stage and width-based layout tests were the model for the scene design.

nodes.label: clawd-spinner prior art
nodes.rationale: One scene per activity and a PNG contact-sheet preview script were the model for the per-state actions and the preview tool.

nodes.label: crab-buddy prior art
nodes.rationale: Raster plus $.ui.blit in-place repaint and one costume per agent type came from this mod.

nodes.label: Hermes petSprite prior art
nodes.rationale: Half-block painter where one cell is two vertical pixels; the technique behind cellsOf.

nodes.label: image-peek prior art
nodes.rationale: Studied for its Image element with real pixels; not used, which is why CrabBus renders cells instead.

nodes.label: savvy-progress prior art
nodes.rationale: Source of the crab drawing, first costume ideas, palette and tier colors (MIT); every sprite was then redrawn by hand at 18 x 14.

nodes.label: Crab rig and pose
nodes.rationale: The body and named anchors (head, face, body, claw, ground, card) give every action a shared frame of reference, so the pose at tick t is computed rather than hand-keyed per frame.

nodes.label: RENDERING.md: how the crabs are drawn
nodes.norm_label: rendering.md: how the crabs are drawn
nodes.rationale: Explains that CrabBus draws everything as terminal cells (Box/Text, Raster, $.ui.blit) with no Image protocol at runtime, and covers the pipeline, preview tool, golden tests, prior art and open items.

nodes.label: Costumes as validated JSON data
nodes.rationale: Costumes and actions are data, so users add designs without code; user JSON is checked by the fit validator before use so a bad design cannot hang or crash the band.

nodes.label: Open: Image mode
nodes.rationale: Real pixels through the Image protocol (Ghostty, kitty, iTerm2) are not verified on screen, so cells remain the renderer; toRgba already produces the pixel bytes that mode would need.

nodes.label: Render pipeline layers
nodes.rationale: Facts, mood, plays, pose, costume, card, scene, cells and paint are separate layers so most of them are pure functions that can be tested; nothing is drawn from anything except recorded facts.

nodes.label: Prior art study
nodes.rationale: Several mods were studied before the renderer was written; CrabBus took techniques and some licensed drawing data, with credits, and never copied code it did not license.

nodes.label: Single blitted stage
nodes.rationale: One Raster for the whole band is repainted in place with $.ui.blit, so each animation frame does not redraw the component tree.
